notes.title: Another Interstellar Visitor | Update 35.3
notes.content:
[p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXda6gfEJDFwUj1cWP9BDCa4p8RbIqgQt3m3IIaET1zWX8g5GXnLIJV_YNjvySPq0XOaSV7BXe6Dbj0vYvvbKtGME649BNXgQ9I8lYIopyH2g26n97ffKw0ajYpwofUV7OG6U1YR?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img][/p][p]Watch the third-ever discovered visitor from outside our Solar System, 3I/ATLAS, fly past the Sun and see how it compares it to other known interstellar interlopers. We’ve also improved the view that shows what parts of the surface of a planet are illuminated, updated our scientific notation, and more![/p][p] [/p][h3]In the Light of Day[/h3][p]The Daylight view now shows surface illumination of a planet in real-time as the object rotates and orbits within the simulation. Previously it was a static snapshot of the daylight on a planet.[/p][p][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdJgjcMECJBIzEjePy8w8ixfXOvSJKh8of_gq9_TkeO4doxNii8LNtJNns1RUKbhhupy_nFMXslSLf8sU7cxU622CHnnSVyUrWg4yRfDCvRJFAUMJK4OR5OGIV7xMIQbSCXRi1A?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img]Before[/p][/td][td][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXexVo7Q9ROdSdxUZoRz0XueEs9qA6cLZLpNeVewzvQ_oKwbXPAgF7UFfhHkbWky-8tWiQNfT_1e-dKw0jLDMA2SxOH_3CoBW1FjCXiNRPwqk2wtRl3mrk7aTQz0tiNcARNR6-ThUw?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img]After[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][h3]Comets from Beyond the Solar System[/h3][p]Watch the comet 3I/ATLAS, the third-ever discovered interstellar visitor to our Solar System, pass by on its journey through space and compare the trajectories of all three known interstellar visitors. Find them under[/p][p][b]Home > Open > Interstellar Comet 31/ATLAS[/b][/p][p][b]Home > Open > Interstellar Object Trajectory Comparison[/b][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdeRcpdDAkyTmBDNcNd7cQq89aIDc9r-KX3eRWdoLHsCmp1FbJUlh53axwxPKdtB_CZpXNXEOLjUqYK15ODwlzFnhWX09GFmcQwAnr2Wia0bJ42s88kgGeFAF5K__g3E6ug_8EY8g?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfUz6Lb0gz7VzVIoTKimdoA4McvdRgJynytPC-q31mw7grrZfMtr1FGwe-iWQLRuKAp67qoqZsb5SstwEuIT4wuru2V7U6LK3qzRvCZcb6WR3vmZWwUpimj6wyGDC2ekevDwuFCQA?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Scientific Notation[/h3][p]Astronomically large (and small) numbers are already hard to understand, so we’ve updated our scientific notation to be friendlier: “1 × 10^#" (previously we used “1E+#”). Try changing Earth’s mass to 1x10^6 Earth masses and see what happens to the Solar System.[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeqllJXoEpPTClnpaQJNtrzD-JOAyStcXWdQarT3-pZaulrGW-MsErtJWmBa6go3ESBYbrACsReqFYEBkGRxO_uS-n2zYZuva7j9AekUa4xXDGH0wyilvj3NFZL1b-5tuvV61vIyA?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img]Before[/p][/td][td][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe42c_2iHAnej9foU4EmxtG2k2KX-pkTsXJHPBuSt8eegBda7fogKimMG33AT9K2U6JZsZiPWv1uEJVbAKlhOSZk5wdQiV0KqKtxHcJ_61oJyNe4GVN_K8BKsnx7tO80Jp4qEZgRw?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img]After[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][h3]More Highlights[/h3][p]Watch what would happen to Earth if the Moon were replaced with a black hole of the same mass or the same radius. Which simulation do you think will be more destructive? Check them out under
[b]Home > Open > Earth with a Black Hole Moon | Same Mass
Home > Open > Earth with a Black Hole Moon | Same Radius
[/b][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdEESx9MW7c91CokdUZSkQumwqiIiTvlfXkcw4HdqVQn2r_GOQ27PiBe-JrDQq6aooWYxr9fZBgrZDs4t6SzPnAdY-V-uDPxtv-K2yT-Yy0M1hNO-SWjreMxTi2w5jJscdGOj1X_w?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]See small objects in your simulation even faster by turning on Markers by pressing “m” (previously “i”) on your keyboard. No need to go all the way to [b]View > Markers[/b]. 
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcpgHR1z_Rlgf6WOGQKsc_9btkjaRtg1qHG5xV8TM7NO36uBdsL1DVQuztkBeT3gOiJdHdp7QLRAj3Xtrj_2GA2871Z-3yp9pu5sFT8sJ6-5s-X2uZE3XgpdqX6HvZz1NnZRncUtg?key=p9KwLNnS_bEk88OoW1Jr0Q"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can once again add custom colors to your human scale objects to make purple cows and pigeon rainbow.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/dd45eb92832cca9cb2f5c4673621218f55d3c15f.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][url="http://universesandbox.com/whatsnew"]Check out the full list of What's New in Update 35.3.[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Please report any issues on our [u][url="http://steamcommunity.com/app/230290/discussions/1/"]Steam forum[/url][/u], [u][url="https://discord.gg/us"]on Discord[/url][/u], or in-game via Home > Send Feedback.[/p]

notes.title: Blinded by the Light | Update 35.2
notes.content:
[p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/VySRMlD.gif"][/img][/p][p]Watch the boiling surface of a star, then set off a supernova and light up your worlds (before your planets are vaporized anyways). Massive stars now leave behind a neutron star or black hole when they end their life with a bang, and much more![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/f2a1209a4af081031d11055ea290311fa4e4a4d2.png"][/img][/p][h3]Super(nova) Lighting[/h3][p]Supernovas now brilliantly light up space as they explode and boil away your planets. Be careful looking at them without your Space Goggles, they’re extremely bright before they realistically fade as they expand and cool down.[/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/t4m1H7L.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]See Stellar Surfaces[/h3][p]Examine the boiling surface of a star. Cells called [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_granule"][u]stellar granules[/u][/url] are created when currents of plasma bring bubbles of superheated materials from the interior to the surface. Star surfaces are too bright for the human eye to see any detail, so we’ve used false colors to make these granules visible. Find it under[/p][p][b]View > Perception > Star Surface Detail[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/0cc9f920c9a24ee4d5161054e5fe13d8ea7a11e9.gif"][/img][/p][h3]
Zombie Stars[/h3][p]Massive stars that go supernova now leave behind a remnant. For stars between 8 and 20 times the mass of the Sun, the remnant is a neutron star. Stars over 20 times the mass of the Sun leave behind a black hole.[/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/XMnbU5Z.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]More Highlights[/h3][p]NASA’s [url="https://science.nasa.gov/mission/lucy/"][u]Lucy spacecraft[/u][/url], named after the [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_(Australopithecus)"][u]Lucy fossil[/u][/url], passed nearby asteroid Donaldjohanson, named after the fossil’s discoverer, on April 20, 2025. This flyby was a test run before Lucy begins its main mission studying the [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jupiter_trojan"][u]Trojan asteroids[/u][/url] that share Jupiter’s orbit. Check out our simulation of the encounter under[/p][p][b]Home > Open > Lucy Spacecraft Encounter with Asteroid Donaldjohanson in 2025[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/42c1a0da590f140ae57e826bbc03cb82c7c35655.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can now smoothly undo the deletion of a large number of objects at once with Ctrl+Z (or Cmd+Z on Mac), and they’ll even have their trails regenerated. You can also undo launching objects.[/p][p][img src="https://i.imgur.com/fyMrgyh.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/c207ef20bbd9f344c09198e6092050a186847d45.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Exoplanet system simulations now include the inclination of known exoplanets around their host stars.[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/8a9e75fc9f85d7719da9f11769d405864a03c226.png"][/img]Before[/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/53f01689c4a4625ae808327332f5d82379d2b843.png"][/img]After[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][/p][p]3D data views no longer color points on the object surface that have a value of zero.[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/daca6f836f9ce4de35ed4c877ad37d4bc2c18cf3.png"][/img]Before[/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/bf2ee8009abac276d58d9f8df276c605cfc3e0fb.png"][/img]After[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][/p][p][url="http://universesandbox.com/whatsnew"]Check out the full list of What's New in Update 35.2.[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Please report any issues on our [url="http://steamcommunity.com/app/230290/discussions/1/"]Steam forum[/url], [url="https://discord.gg/us"]on Discord[/url], or in-game via Home > Send Feedback.[/p]

notes.title: Describing the Universe | Update 35.1
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/pPaVBgp.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/fe75027b73ed419d5df35a69251b444cb2504d68.png[/img]

[h4]Describe Your Worlds[/h4]
Add rich details to any object and the simulation itself with the new description properties. Include your favorite facts about each planet in the Solar System, or give a detailed backstory to your custom Tatooine! Add them under
[*][b]Object Properties > Overview > Description[/b]
[*][b]Simulation > Description[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/08ae828f3e5a95cc1e0251e2df00d53b142f5589.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/c9dc8fc978d8b85e4650d580c4bf259058129550.png[/img]

[h4]Choose Your Startup Simulation[/h4]
Pick up where you left off and have Universe Sandbox open your most recent save, your own custom work in progress, or any of our included simulations when it starts up. Set this under
[b]Home > Settings > General > Experience > Startup Simulation
[/b]This feature was added in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/230290/view/527587373100302497]Space in a New Light | Update 35[/url], but wanted to highlight it again in case you missed it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/c1e115e92a4e9978e64a4a0a9736fca3af102363.gif[/img]

[h4]Visualizing Planet Data[/h4]
See information about your planets, like the Surface Temperature or Elevation, projected on their surfaces in 3D. This view is now shown in the object preview and on the objects in the simulation. Check it out under
[b]Object Properties > Visuals > Surface[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/a25a5d3f5816e78dc0b1edf2381a44586614536f.gif[/img]

[h4]More Highlights[/h4]
Use the new actions in the View panel to Fly, Land, reset the camera position, and more.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/l0YMmhS.gif[/img]


Controls to show and hide an object's atmosphere, clouds, and dust clouds are now simulation-wide view settings instead of only applying when zoomed in on an object. Find them in the View panel.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/03a3324f0be04a5011a4481c4951e0350bf82a79.gif[/img]


The simulation of exoplanet [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K2-18b]K2-18 b[/url] has been updated to reflect the recent [url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3847/2041-8213/adc1c8]evidence of specific molecules[/url] in K2-18 b's atmosphere that are known to be produced by biological processes on Earth. However, some scientists have argued these molecules may be produced without life, and more data is needed to confirm these molecules are really present in K2-18 b's atmosphere.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/d2286b84dc98c3ec086db96cdbd67b4bd3100a50.png[/img]

[url=http://universesandbox.com/whatsnew" data-type="URL" data-id="http://universesandbox.com/whatsnew]Check out the full list of What's New in Update 35.1.[/url]

Please report any issues on our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/230290/discussions/1/]Steam forum[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/us]on Discord[/url], or in-game via Home > Send Feedback.

notes.title: Universe Sandbox Roadmap: 2025 & Beyond
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/aef24e3887265dee25b73e4636e207d9abf5ff1a.gif[/img]
We started 2025 by releasing our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/527587373100302498]major graphics overhaul[/url], but we have much more planned for the year, including allowing meteors to burn up in an atmosphere, simulating basic life, and getting Universe Sandbox on mobile devices so you can create and destroy on the go. Before diving into details, let’s look back on some highlights from 2024.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/2834962d413c258d80aafb350d06a5276981b57c.png[/img]
[h2 class="wp-block-heading"]Highlights from 2024[/h2]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/OGhpqVB.gif[/img]
[i]The Moon’s shadow passing over Earth during the total solar eclipse across North America on April 8, 2024.[/i]

We spent 2024 working on our major graphics overhaul, released March 2025, and many of the other in-progress features mentioned in this roadmap. In addition to the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/4164221872003651015]awe-inspiring realistic graphics[/url], our March graphics update included many [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/4452466204163967747]quality-of-life improvements[/url]. Our biggest accomplishments from the year include:
[list]
[*]Improving material simulation and manipulation with more realistic atmosphere colors and opacity and the ability to swap one material for another. ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/4196862191894981139]Update 34.1[/url], March 2024)
[*]Replacing our 10-year-old graphics technology with a state-of-the-art system so you can immerse yourself in a more awe-inspiring and realistic universe. ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/527587373100302498/]Update 35[/url], March 2025)
[*]Implementing a new interface system that automatically positions, resizes, and closes panels so you can focus on manipulating the universe instead of managing panels. ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/527587373100302498]Update 35[/url], March 2025)
[/list]
The new graphics rendering and user interface systems were major milestones on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/6501581293008131628/]2024 Roadmap[/url].

[h2 class="wp-block-heading"]What’s the Plan for 2025?[/h2]
[list]
[*]✅Finish our major graphics update.
[list]
[*]Released on March 3, 2025!
[/list]
[*]Add basic life simulation where vegetation grows, dies, and gets eaten.
[*]Optimize and rewrite our simulation using Unity’s [url=https://unity.com/dots]Data-Oriented Technology Stack (DOTS)[/url].
[*]Bring Universe Sandbox to phones and tablets (iOS & Android).
[/list]
We plan to work on all these projects in 2025, but some, like getting Universe Sandbox on mobile devices, have been in the works for years. Additional challenges may arise that delay features, and our priorities may change.

[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]Even More Graphics Improvements: The Saga Continues[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/UUnmo8S.gif[/img][i]
A comparison of Earth and 100 Colliding Moons showing how much more realistic the scenario looks in our new graphics update.[/i]

Earlier this year, we [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/230290/announcements/detail/4452466204163967360]released our major graphics update[/url] with hot, non-stellar objects emitting light, physically based lighting, and more. But we’re not done yet! We’re planning even more graphics features, including object selection highlights that are unique to the object’s shape and new point light object.
[list]
[*]But Wait, There’s More!
[list]
[*]Now that our new graphics rendering system is out, we’re planning to utilize it to add even more graphics features, including
[list]
[*]Redesigning object selection outlines to be more visible, useful, and unique to that object’s shape instead of always being a circle.
[*]Adding new Point Lights with customizable colors to light up your simulations without adding stars (and boiling Earth) for that perfect shot.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/i0cRYES.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress: Point Lights are a work in progress that allows you to customize your simulation's lighting further.[/i]

[*]Simulating supernovas emitting light (Spoiler - they’re really [i]really[/i] bright).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/d17691a4256809bd33716dec86fa68ff2cc58353.png[/img][i]Work in Progress: A supernova lighting up a few different objects, including Jupiter and a very large banana. Space Goggles are On because the supernova is so bright.[/i]
[/list]
[/list]
[/list]
[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]Life Simulation: Let There Be Life![/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/38d1223af19077270b2f9a00b550452e62c52e71.png[/img][i]Work in Progress: The work-in-progress life simulation interface tracks the mass of vegetation, herbivores, and non-living matter, and the habitability of each point on a planet's surface.[/i]

Last year, we began working on life simulation after adding materials like carbon dioxide and oxygen to planet atmospheres. Vegetation will grow, spread, die, and be eaten on planet surfaces, similarly to how we simulate temperature, liquid, and gas flow.
[list]
[*]Simulating Vegetation
[list]
[*]Life can spread to other planets on fragments from collisions.
[*]As vegetation grows and dies, the amount of carbon dioxide and oxygen in the atmosphere will change.
[*]Vegetation will grow, spread, and die based on the local conditions on the surface of a planet.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/272b68b7c234cf972767a4aeb8a3b9e523da3411.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress: All life on Earth is killed, only to reseed it with some vegetation using the Planetscaping tool. The vegetation slowly spreads back across Earth.[/i]

[*]You’ll be able to customize the conditions needed for life on your planets so your plants can absorb methane and emit hydrogen, for example.
[list]
[*]You can even set the conditions to make life grow on Titan!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/255256f4080d3766dfbedcd28a698f60e4134e09.png[/img][i]Work in Progress: Custom vegetation thriving on the surface of Saturn’s Moon Titan after setting the temperature range and atmosphere pressure to match Titan’s surface and having it take in methane and output oxygen.[/i]
[/list]
[/list]
[*]Animals & the Circle of Life
[list]
[*]Herbivores, like vegetation, will also be simulated on planet surfaces. The overall herbivore mass will be tracked and will also depend on how much vegetation there is on the planet to support them.
[*]The names and life requirements of the two species will be customizable as well, so you can let your imagination run wild to simulate your favorite plants and animals, like cows, trees, whales, [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dik-dik]dik-diks[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplocarpus_foetidus]skunk cabbage[/url], aliens, unicorns, you name it (literally)!
[/list]
[*]Future Models
[list]
[*]We plan to make our food chain even more complex with carnivores in the future.
[*]You’ll be able to quickly cause catastrophic events leading to mass extinctions. For now, we have a simple Kill All Life action.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/b27c20ea655b8f69daed9d447463989552f62601.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress: Kill all life on a planet with the press of a button.[/i]
[/list][/list]
[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]Advanced Physics Technology[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/qGSErXS.gif[/img][i]
Work in Progress: Earth is orbited by eight Ceres, which get stretched and ripped apart by Earth’s tidal forces, forming rings around the planet.[/i]

Improving collisions with more realistic friction and craters, simulating atmospheric drag, which allows meteors to burn up in the atmosphere, and continuing to optimize our physics simulation are all things we're working on this year.
[list]
[*]Advanced Game Engine Features
[list]
[*]We’re continuing to reconstruct our simulation architecture using the [url=https://unity.com/dots]Data-Oriented Technology Stack (DOTS)[/url] from Unity, the game engine we use to build Universe Sandbox. We’re excited about the expected performance gains and future opportunities it brings. We plan to roll these changes out in multiple phases.
[list]
[*]Phase 1 replaces our current physics engine with a new DOTS-based system that will make Universe Sandbox easier to maintain and improve.
[list]
[*]Upgrading to DOTS in phase 1 lays the foundation for everyday, non-spherical object collisions (like two dice), building and flying spacecraft, and constructing megastructures like [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyson_sphere]Dyson spheres[/url].
[/list]
[*]Phase 2 will unify our collision simulation to allow for more realistic collisions of celestial objects like planets and everyday objects like pigeons. This phase will allow
[list]
[*]Objects to physically deform due to craters, fragmentation, laser impacts, and more, influencing how they collide.
[*]Everyday objects, including simple shapes like dice and complex shapes like spacecraft, to collide according to their unique forms instead of as spheres, also called rigid-body physics.
[/list]
[/list]
[/list]
[*]DOTS optimizes our simulation by efficiently running more computations simultaneously on the CPU, allowing for more objects, collisions, and fragments.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/yaWmo43.gif[/img][i]Current[/i]
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/IFs4YwL.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress[/i]
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/list]
[*]New Gravity Simulation
[list]
[*]We’re experimenting with a new method of gravity simulation, called [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnes%E2%80%93Hut_simulation]Barnes-Hut simulation[/url], to allow rock fragments and dust clouds to attract and merge, forming planets & moons. Currently, these particles can only be pulled on and cannot form planets independently.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/pSL2You.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress: The red boxes show how the gravity tree used in Barnes-Hut simulation divides up space dynamically into chunks of particles to more efficiently simulate the intersections between thousands of particles instead of constantly brute force computing the gravitational interactions between all objects. You can see the boxes change as fragments are created and spread out in space.[/i]
[/list]
[*]Grinding to a Halt
[list]
[*]Our new friction model will simulate craters stretching out as objects skid across each other’s surfaces during collisions. In our current simplistic model, craters are always circular.
[/list]
[*]Visually Deformed Objects
[list]
[*]Most objects in Universe Sandbox are spheres, but in real life, some rotate so quickly that they stretch and flatten, like the dwarf planet [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haumea]Haumea[/url]. We’re working to simulate this stretching visually.
[list]
[*]This will not affect the object's physical shape, collisions, or surface simulation until after Phase 2 of our restructuring our simulation with DOTS is complete.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/osStR0D.gif[/img][i]Current[/i]
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/91lEfsy.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress[/i]
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/list]
[/list]
[*]Atmospheric Drag
[list]
[*]To simulate meteors, we’re working on adding a drag force so objects burn up while traveling through a planet’s atmosphere. Currently, objects pass through atmospheres unchanged.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3BapE0y.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress: A small asteroid burns up as it travels through an atmosphere before crashing into the surface.[/i]
[/list]
[*]Tidal Locking
[list]
[*]We’re planning to simulate objects becoming [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_locking]tidally locked[/url], where the same side of one always faces the other as they orbit each other, like the Moon to the Earth.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/924d0e04b7df339398180444590d616f82087177.gif[/img][i]Current[/i]
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/08959556b2959655dac72e6ba7daed834d136122.gif[/img][i]Work in Progress[/i]
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/list]
[*]Mathematical Points
[list]
[*]We’re planning to add more visualizations of useful mathematical points and boundaries, including
[*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagrange_point]Lagrange Points[/url] - the points where the gravitational influence of two objects is equally strong. Objects placed at these points orbit in a stationary position relative to the two objects like the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Webb_Space_Telescope]James Webb Space Telescope[/url] is to Earth and the Sun.
[*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_sphere]Hill Spheres[/url] - the boundary within which a moon is gravitationally bound to a planet.
[*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roche_limit]Roche Limit[/url] - the boundary where the tidal forces pulling on an orbiting object are stronger than its self-gravity, ripping it apart.
[/list]
[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]Universe Sandbox on Phones & Tablets[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/eaiCY28.gif[/img][i]
Universe Sandbox in portrait mode with our new dynamic interface system that automatically positions, resizes, and closes panels so you can always see the simulation.[/i]

Getting Universe Sandbox on mobile devices (iOS & Android) is a major focus again this year. We’ve made a lot of progress with our new graphics update and interface system, which significantly improves usability on small touchscreens, but there’s still a lot to do.
[list]
[*]Small Screen Interface
[list]
[*]Our new interface system automatically positions, resizes, and closes panels so you can always see the simulation. This system optimizes interface usability for any screen size, from small touch screens to ultrawide monitors and we’re planning to continue improving and polishing it this year.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/XNUVt9o.gif[/img][i]Before[/i]
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9SVyb3S.gif[/img][i]After[/i]
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[/list]
[*]Running the Universe
[list]
[*]Boosting performance across all platforms is another mobile requirement. We’ve been improving interface responsiveness, resource utilization, and optimizing start-up times.
[*]Rebuilding our simulation architecture will also bring necessary performance boosts to desktop and mobile devices alike.
[/list]
[*]Automated Test Suite
[list]
[*]We’re expanding our automated tests, which cover collision physics, simulation performance, and more, and the ways we compare their results, to help us catch and fix bugs across desktop and mobile devices faster.
[/list]
[*]More Information
[list]
[*]Universe Sandbox on mobile is built from the same codebase as the desktop version and will have the same features.
[*]There is no mobile release date yet.
[*]We plan on it being a one-time paid app with no ads or in-game purchases.
[list]
[*]Price is not finalized.
[/list]
[*]Minimum requirements are not finalized.
[*]Sign up for our mobile mailing list to receive updates about mobile development
[url=http://universesandbox.com/mobile/]http://universesandbox.com/mobile/[/url]
[/list]
[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]And Beyond[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3UKOw1X.gif[/img]
[i]Experimental Tests: Adding more detailed planet surfaces show the planet getting more detailed as you zoom in. This is a very early prototype.[/i]

Our future goals include adding detailed planet surfaces, simulating the life cycle of a star, and allowing you to use custom elevation maps and textures on your planets. These are in early development, and we don’t know when they will be released.
[list]
[*]Detailed Planet Surfaces
[list]
[*]Imagine flying over mountains and through canyons on planet surfaces in Universe Sandbox. We’re still experimenting with ways to add more details to planet surfaces, but we’re excited about the possibilities.
[/list]
[*]Planet Customization
[list]
[*]We want to give you even more control over planet appearances. Satisfy your world-building desires and create a planet using custom maps or images, like a picture of your dog.
[/list]
[*]Stellar Lifecycles
[list]
[*]Realistically simulating how stars burn hydrogen into helium (and heavier elements) and die violent deaths is complex, but we’re planning to rebuild our star simulation so we can bring stellar evolution to Universe Sandbox.
[/list]
[*]Volatiles
[list]
[*]To simulate comet tails streaking through space, we plan to overhaul our volatile system, which determines how gas escapes from a planet’s atmosphere into space.
[/list]
[*]Gamepad and Steam Deck
[list]
[*]What could be better than playing Universe Sandbox from the comfort of your couch? We’re working on adding gamepad support for more ways to control your universe. This will improve our Steam Deck support and has the potential to support other gamepad-based consoles in the future.
[/list]
[/list]
We’re excited to bring so much to Universe Sandbox this year, and we can’t wait to share it with you!

notes.title: Space in a New Light | Update 35
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/UUnmo8S.gif[/img]
Immerse yourself in a universe more awe-inspiring and realistic than ever before with our next-generation graphics update! We've also added many interface improvements to make controlling the universe easier and more intuitive. You need to see it to believe it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/198839bc35b7d54dbb5d0a23fa423ef225b4b226.png[/img]

[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]A More Realistic Graphics Engine[/h4]
We’ve completely replaced our 10-year-old graphics technology with a state-of-the-art system to make Universe Sandbox look more realistic with physically-based lighting. This new system has required us to update our [url=https://universesandbox.com/faq/#system]minimum requirements[/url]. [url=https://universesandbox.com/blog/2024/11/next-gen-graphics-update/]Learn more[/url].

[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/uBMlO8X.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/uUQa9W7.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]Edit Objects Simultaneously[/h4]
The properties panel now lets you edit multiple objects at once. Use the new [b]Multi-Select[/b] tool to select multiple objects and try increasing the mass of every object in the Solar System simultaneously!
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/e755029e6fac2db843d48c6485f5c867ff068e82.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/lsYDZ20.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]Automatic Interface Management[/h4]
Focus on manipulating the universe instead of managing panels with our new interface system that automatically positions, resizes, and closes panels so you can always see the simulation. This immersive system also provides better support for ultrawide monitors and small screens (like smartphones).
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/XNUVt9o.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9SVyb3S.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]More Highlights[/h4]

[b]Focus on realism[/b]
Making Universe Sandbox look as realistic as possible with physically-based lighting has made stars realistically bright, and collisions result in blindingly realistic hot spots. It turns out there’s a reason you’re not supposed to look at the Sun.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/39152c1883a1a2e067771e1671f28597211cecb3.png[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/cf223756d798fcea5848dadab7be222c11b27089.png[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/bb7e259c0ca9e3e39028f723f1cbc191f4798453.png[/img]

Light from hot planets
Hot objects now emit light based on their temperature so you can use intense impacts to light up your simulation. Previously, only stars could emit light.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/tPi0I0K.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/EgCB7m0.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Localized glow
Objects now bloom only in hot areas, like those created from lasers or collisions, instead of being surrounded by a single uniform glow.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/87b8fc7c59f076e0f5a42759219fd20017933cb9.png[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/c76aa7846ec9df7b35d2cbeb0fd84e1067e68747.png[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Smoothly blending clouds
Gas and dust clouds now smoothly pass over planets instead of creating sharp intersections.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/2658cfc4a5b5c7f19a4e1704f9cc68dab774571b.png[/img]Before

    [/tr]
[/table]
Realistic artifacts
The surfaces of human-scale objects, or artifacts like spacecraft, have shiny, reflective metals and rough, rugged edges that interact with light more realistically.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/9a4a68c87b4a4a43b1c3ab0bd9e520ad54471d95.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/AXLwHFx.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Math in text fields
All object properties now support basic math. Try typing “*42” into a property to multiply by 42 or “/3” to divide by 3, for example.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/8f6907772ca637c087cd3affa1a5a17617b44144.gif[/img]

Explore planet surfaces
Move across the surface of a planet with the WASD keys after landing on it by zooming in for a closer look or using the Land action button in the planet's Overview tab.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/1CFZBCn.gif[/img]

Light intensity with distance
Objects are now always realistically lit based on their physical distance from a light source. Previously, objects were lit with the same intensity based on the camera's distance from a light source instead of the object's distance from a light source.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/ca009c4f470b852ce477d9eaec624216640c24f3.png[/img]Before (Realistic Object Visibility): Planet sizes have been exaggerated to show how planets are all lit at the same intensity, no matter how far they are from the Sun.
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/a9cc8b3956b4bb17fdbb12214d3dc25609200316.png[/img]After (Realistic Lighting with Space Goggle On): Planet sizes have been exaggerated to show how planets are lit more realistically based on their distance from the Sun.
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Light warping
Black holes now realistically warp the visuals from other black holes instead of blocking any black holes behind them from being seen. The images below are from the same simulation, with custom colors in the “Before” image that make the black holes easier to see.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/8129542239ac0290fec7fc649b80dfd032422b3e.png[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/a73cfd1bb98cc18fa3cbd867ba01884c0adabe74.png[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Updated View Panel
We’ve improved the View panel with more intuitive controls and lighting options
[*]You can now see and change the camera target from the View panel.
[*]Space Goggles provide a more comfortable view that filters the brightness to show the action while preserving realism. Turning them off switches to an unfiltered realistic view where stars, hot objects, and collisions can be blindingly bright.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/82db79723167791f17ae87514d474aafc585c7ed.png[/img]
Before

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/495fb21acf5250c4b9743a1e46a74d9e076bbc1c.png[/img]
After

Action Buttons
We’ve added all-new Action buttons at the top of every Properties tab. Quickly fly to a planet or explode it. Your call. (These buttons replace the Action tab.)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/96d29fcad190ac464cfc478cb663c60853041ebd.png[/img]

[*]Save objects or learn more about real astronomical ones with our new Wikipedia button under Additional Actions.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/c80adf4444b49303e08ede4b5febf1dc66a83170.png[/img]

Color maps
We’ve updated our Data View color maps to make them more perceptually uniform. We've also added colorblind-friendly color maps and the ability to invert them.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/b0e953b4b917cfed8071cfe371a0b63315281e82.png[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/6304cd4d7002028f7bb9ca065fd9865d355b3909.png[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/dd3798038caa6fc709ff1b6c9f215eabbf703a76.png[/img]

Inspecting the surface
Use the new Inspect tool to quickly see the temperature, material composition, elevation, and other properties of specific points on a planet’s surface.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/5427cb8effd0f4f491f8b7d0975e008c59d6e7f6.gif[/img]

Selectable Orbital Parent
It’s now easier to create binary systems orbiting a common center of mass (also called a barycenter). View and adjust an object's Orbital Elements around a binary by selecting the system's barycenter as the object’s Orbital Parent.
[table]
    [tr]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/4f65e2586d95dcc89af47b1ce07c558c8cfb4019.gif[/img]Before
        [/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/bd70b823b7092921f780567f0688450443f3a28b.gif[/img]After
        [/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Choose your Startup Simulation
Choose the simulation that automatically opens when Universe Sandbox starts, from any of our included simulations to your own custom work in progress. Just go to
[b]Home > Settings > General > Experience > Startup Simulation[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/e7b77c0b0f3880fe09b6de4261e9818415a52119.png[/img]

New hotbar
The hotbar has been overhauled so you can add even more shortcuts to manipulate the universe. To edit your hotbar, go to Settings > General > Edit Hotbar or right-click on it and then select “Edit Hotbar.”
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4425618/fcba6ae5a58d2b7ccaaed794a5dee20695bc6cb2.gif[/img]

A Potentially Dangerous Asteroid
Watch the projected path of one of the most potentially dangerous asteroids ever detected, YR 2024, as it flies near Earth in 2032, or check out a What If? scenario of what the impact might look like under
[b]Close Encounter of Asteroid YR4 2024 with Earth in 2032[/b]
And
[b]What If Asteroid YR4 2024 Collides with Earth in 2032?[/b]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/toB3pI4.gif[/img]

[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]New Minimum Requirements[/h4]
Improving our graphics means we need to update our minimum hardware requirements to include
[*]4 GB dedicated video memory (up from 2 GB). 8 GB is recommended.
[*]4 GB RAM (up from 2 GB). 8 GB is recommended.
[*]4 GB of free disk space (up from 2 GB).

Windows:
[*]DirectX 12 
[*]Windows 10 21H1+ (support for Windows 7 SP1, 8, 8.1, and older versions of Windows 10 will be dropped)

Apple:
[*]Silicon (M1 or newer). Intel Mac will no longer be supported. Universe Sandbox may still run on Intel-based Macs, but we cannot guarantee good performance for every Intel-based Mac.
[*]macOS 11.0+ (support for macOS 10.14 and 10.15 will be dropped)

While it is never fun to have support dropped, this new graphics system will allow us to improve performance and add new features to Universe Sandbox now and well into the future.

We’ll ensure all users affected by this change can always access the version of Universe Sandbox from before this minimum requirements update. [url=https://universesandbox.com/support/oldversions" data-type="link" data-id="https://universesandbox.com/support/oldversions]Learn how[/url].

[url=http://universesandbox.com/whatsnew]Check out the full list of What's New in Update 35.[/url]

Please report any issues on our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/230290/discussions/1/]Steam forum[/url], [url=https://discord.gg/us]on Discord[/url], or in-game via Home > Send Feedback.

notes.title: Space in a New Light Preview Now Available | Major Graphics Update
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/nDPoiSn.gif[/img]
Immerse yourself in a universe more awe-inspiring and realistic than ever before with our next-generation Universe Sandbox graphics update. We’ve spent the last two years completely replacing our 10-year-old graphics technology with a state-of-the-art system in our biggest update in years and our biggest visual update ever!
[list]
[*]Our new graphics engine is a vastly improved realistic rendering system that’s more robust, easier to improve, and lets us better show you how the universe really looks.
[*]Doubling down on realism brought a new set of technical and design challenges for us to tackle to make every aspect of Universe Sandbox as realistic as possible.
[*]We’ve completely ripped out our old graphic engine replacing thousands of lines of code.
[/list]
We’ve also included many non-graphics-related improvements with this update, including
[list]
[*]A new interface system that automatically positions, resizes, and closes panels so you can always see the simulation.
[*]Editing multiple objects at once in the Properties panel. To select multiple objects, hold down Control (⌘ on Mac) and click on each object you want to include.
[list]
[*]All object properties now support basic math.
[/list]
[*]New Action buttons at the top of every Properties tab instead of an Actions tab so you can quickly fly to a planet or explode it.
[/list]

This graphics update is part of [url=https://universesandbox.com/blog/2024/03/universe-sandbox-roadmap-2024/]our plan[/url] to rewrite Universe Sandbox piece by piece with cutting-edge systems so we can continue to improve it for years to come. It’s like we’re gradually replacing every part of a spaceship out from under you while you’re actively piloting it.

[h4 class="wp-block-heading"]Space in a New Light | Update 35 is now out![/h4]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/230290/view/527587373100302497]Learn more[/url] about all the additions and improvements in this update.

[h3 class="wp-block-heading"]A Brighter Future For All (Literally)[/h3]
While not exhaustive, some of the most visually apparent changes you’ll see in Universe Sandbox are
[list]
[*]Focus on realism
Making Universe Sandbox look as realistic as possible with physically-based lighting has brought new challenges. For example, stars can now be realistically bright.
